title: the item reference count overflows and the item is freed with its holders still holding it
consumer: memcached.c, process_get_command()'s multiget loop, through items.c do_item_get
live_proof: the fix is in the pinned tree: IT_REFCOUNT_LIMIT 60000 at memcached.c:2185, applied through limited_get and limited_get_locked, which proto_parser.c, proto_bin.c and proto_text.c all call. The case reconstructs the pre-fix path, in which do_item_get incremented without a ceiling
object: an item, i.e. one chunk of a slab class, referenced once per occurrence of its key in the multiget
lifetime_ender: do_item_remove (items.c:538) when the wrapped count reaches zero: item_free -> slabs_free, and the chunk goes on its class's slots list (slabs.c:501), never to free()
shape: reference count overflow / item freed with holders remaining / slabs reuse / read through the dead pointer
allocator_layer: slabs.c size classes over 1 MiB pages, memcached 1.6.45
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator: slabs.c is upstream's file at the 1.6.45 pin and makes every allocation decision. The item layer is reduced to item_free and do_item_remove with their arithmetic verbatim; the hash table, the LRU queues, the stats and the locks are left out because none of them takes part in the decision to free. The 65536 references are taken for real, one at a time, so the wrap is performed rather than asserted
distinguishing: the corpus's only case with a CVE and distribution advisories behind it, and the only one whose cause is an arithmetic limit rather than a control-flow mistake: nobody wrote a wrong line. unsigned short simply stopped counting
sibling_issue: the same overflow was still reachable through the binary protocol until e3b7d33 (2026-07-02), which upstream describes as a remote-code-execution path, and the meta protocol was hardened separately in bc080ab (2020-02-27). One defect, three front ends, nine years

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host: the sequence COMPLETES. exit=0, completed=1, object_reuses=0, chunk_reuses=1. Not caught. The reuse counters are the point: the storage really was handed back out, which is the situation revocation would have to catch if the memory reached free(). It does not -- cache.c keeps it on its own STAILQ and slabs.c returns it to the page, so libc's quarantine never holds it. EVIDENCE COMMITTED 2026-10-06: results/20261006-cheribsd/. Both controls are in that bundle -- the revocation control FAULTED with addr == pc == the independently resolved expectation (0x101e42), proving the revoker sweeps in this guest AND attributing the fault; and a NEGATIVE CONTROL run on the same vehicle makes all 8 case oracles FAIL while the three platform controls still pass, so none of these completions is vacuous. The image hash is byte-identical to the vehicle the ffmpeg readings of the same day used, so the two programs' columns are comparable. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-cheribsd-fixed-buggy/ (R1): buggy and FIXED arms, same program, same boot, both complete; the revocation control faulted at its labelled load in that boot.
cheribsd-revocation.control: the control fired in the SAME boot: revocation-control exit=162 signal=34 (SIGPROT) si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) with pc == the address the supervisor resolved independently (0x101e42). The platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds passed in the same run.

NOT the PoisonCap platform the 2026-09-21 bundles used, so those hashes differ by construction.

native-detect.requires: the chunk never reaches free(), so ASan has no event; it would see the reuse only as an ordinary live object
native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -g; port library with the same sanitizer). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 67108864` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 67108864` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (3ef5169ae90b); the arm was previously 'not written'.
native-detect.measured: 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-native-asan-stock-malloc/run-asan.txt: SILENT -- the defect reproduced (VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED) and ASan printed nothing; built with MCP_STOCK_MALLOC=ON (each page and cache.c object its own malloc, as upstream); both controls reported in the same run

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm lets the count wrap, so the first two releases free an item 65536 clients still hold, the next slabs_alloc returns the same chunk, and the holder reads the other item's bytes; the fixed arm answers the get as a miss at the limit and the count never wraps
native-fix-differential.note: unit_reissued differs between the arms, as in case 2: the premature free IS the defect, so the control cannot show the reuse it enables

sublet-malloc.target: Capstone domain, the allocators port's ledger in mode 2: stock slabs.c/cache.c on Sublet as the SYSTEM allocator -- a chunk carries its whole page's bound, an object its own, and nothing is revoked until a page or object is given back
sublet-malloc.oracle: the sequence completes: the refcount wrap frees the chunk into its class's free list, not to free() MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-sublet-malloc/: the sequence COMPLETES, NOT CAUGHT (completed=1, image 97da40cdb1541f17).

CheriBSD MEASURED 2026-10-06 on a vehicle built on this host, revocation on, 8/8 arms passed and 0 of 8 caught; run summaries stay outside the repository by this corpus's policy, so the reading is here. ASan measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-native-asan/): NOT CAUGHT.
note: damage is the holder reading another item's bytes where it stored its own. Upstream's issue #271 reports the other consequence of the same free -- the hash chain closing on itself, h_next == it, and assoc_find looping forever
nested_why: memcached's slab allocator carved the object out of a 1 MiB page it owns -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NESTED.
